pointers.sentence: `Sitemap._get` gives `None` for one the sitemap lacks, calls a callable with the item, and otherwise returns the value (`django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py:Sitemap._get`).

`Sitemap._urls` makes a dictionary for each item of the page asked for, with the keys `"item"`, `"location"`, `"lastmod"`, `"changefreq"`, `"priority"` and `"alternates"`; the location joins the protocol, the domain and the path, and the priority is a string, empty for none (`django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py:Sitemap._urls`).
`Sitemap.paginator` makes a new `Paginator` of the items, `limit` to a page, each time it is read, calling `items` again (`django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py:Sitemap.paginator`).

`Sitemap.get_urls` takes a page, a site and a protocol. The protocol is `Sitemap.get_protocol`'s: the sitemap's own `Sitemap.protocol`, else the one passed, else `"https"`. The domain is `Sitemap.get_domain`'s: the site passed, else the current site by `SITE_ID`; without the sites application or that row, `ImproperlyConfigured`, "To use sitemaps, either enable the sites framework or pass a Site/RequestSite object in your view." (`django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py:Sitemap.get_domain`). The `sitemap` view always passes the request's site and scheme, so the `"https"` and the lookup serve code that builds a sitemap outside a request.

`Sitemap._items` makes the pairs of item and code before pagination, so that, its comment says, pages are cut with every language counted: `limit` counts URLs, not objects (`django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py:Sitemap._items`).

`_get` hands a method the object alone, and `Sitemap._location` calls `location` inside `django.utils.translation.override` of the pair's language, so under `i18n_patterns` `reverse` writes that language's prefix (`django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py:Sitemap._location`) ([The active language](../i18n/active-language.md), [Language prefixes and translated routes](../urls/i18n.md)).

With `Sitemap.alternates` also true, each URL links to the item in each of its languages, and with `Sitemap.x_default` once more, as `"x-default"`, when `LANGUAGE_CODE` is among them: the URL in that language with the first path segment that is its code cut out (`django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py:Sitemap._urls`).

`priority`, `changefreq` and `protocol` may be passed as arguments, and count only where the class's own value is false, such as `None` (`django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py:GenericSitemap.__init__`).

The index asks each sitemap for `Sitemap.get_latest_lastmod`, which returns a `lastmod` that is a value, and calls one that is a method on every item and takes the greatest; `None` if it has none or some item's is `None` (`django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py:Sitemap.get_latest_lastmod`).
`GenericSitemap.get_latest_lastmod`, given a `"date_field"`, asks the database for one value, and otherwise returns `None` (`django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py:GenericSitemap.get_latest_lastmod`).

Both take the domain from `get_current_site` and the protocol from the request's scheme unless a sitemap sets its own ([Sites: `Site`, `get_current_site` and the `shortcut` view](sites.md)), return a `TemplateResponse` of `"sitemap_index.xml"` or `"sitemap.xml"` by default, as `"application/xml"` ([`SimpleTemplateResponse` and `TemplateResponse`](../templates/responses.md)), and are wrapped by `x_robots_tag`, which sets X-Robots-Tag to `"noindex, noodp, noarchive"` (`django/contrib/sitemaps/views.py:x_robots_tag`).

`index` reverses the URL its sitemap_url_name argument names, by default `"django.contrib.sitemaps.views.sitemap"`, with the section as `"section"`, and makes a `SitemapIndexItem` of the absolute URL and the sitemap's `get_latest_lastmod`; each page after the first adds the URL with `"?p="` and the page's number, and the same date (`django/contrib/sitemaps/views.py:index`).
The page is the query string's `"p"`, 1 by default, asked of every sitemap rendered; the paginator's `EmptyPage` and `PageNotAnInteger` become `Http404` (`django/contrib/sitemaps/views.py:sitemap`).
`_get_latest_lastmod` keeps the greatest, a date taken as midnight and a naive datetime as UTC (`django/contrib/sitemaps/views.py:_get_latest_lastmod`).
So that `ConditionalGetMiddleware` can answer 304 Not Modified, the comment at each header says ([Cache headers and conditional requests: `django/utils/cache.py`](../services/http-caching.md)).

It asks for the current site without the request, so needs `SITE_ID` even where the views find the site by host, and raises `ImproperlyConfigured` without the sites application (`django/contrib/flatpages/sitemaps.py:FlatPageSitemap.items`) ([Flat pages and redirects: the fallback middleware](flatpages-and-redirects.md)).
